field.note: No Wikipedia article for the center under its name or its 2023 name; no redirect; a full-text search of articles for the quoted phrases 'AI Tracking Center' and 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' returns no result. The operator's article (raw wikitext B6.wiki, rendered B6.html/B6.txt) has a section 'Disinformation in AI' (the chatbot audits) and none on the center, its catalogue or content farms; the strings 'Tracking Center', 'content farm' and 'UAIN' are absent from the wikitext and the rendered text. Its short description files NewsGuard as a browser plugin. Outside this origin, not ledgered: Wikipedia's 'Content farm' article names a 2023 NewsGuard report on brands supporting AI-driven content farms (found by a control search for "NewsGuard" "content farm", which also returned Pink-slime journalism and three other articles); it does not name the center.

F1.quote: This AI Tracking Center is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news.
F1.claim: what it is, in its own words: a center highlighting how generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news
F1.lineage: what it is: generative AI in misinformation and unreliable news

F2.quote: The Center includes a selection of NewsGuard’s reports, insights, and debunks related to artificial intelligence.
F2.claim: it includes a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports, insights and debunks
F2.lineage: what it holds: a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports, insights and debunks

F3.quote: From unreliable AI-generated news outlets operating with little to no human oversight, to fabricated images produced by AI image generators, the rollout of generative artificial intelligence tools has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike.
F3.claim: the rollout of generative AI has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors
F3.lineage: the occasion: generative AI and content farms

F4.quote: To date, NewsGuard’s team has identified 3,749 AI Content Farm news and information websites spanning 16 languages: Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Dutch, English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Turkish.
F4.claim: the count: 3,749 AI Content Farm sites in 16 languages, named

F5.quote: Coverage by McKenzie Sadeghi, Dimitris Dimitriadis, Virginia Padovese, Giulia Pozzi, Sara Badilini, Chiara Vercellone, Natalie Huet, Zack Fishman, Leonie Pfaller, and Natalie Adams | Last Updated June 23, 2026
F5.claim: compiled by ten named NewsGuard analysts; last updated 23 June 2026

F6.quote: These websites – which typically feature generic names such as Times Business News and Business Post – also tend to churn out dozens of articles a day and are often the originators of false claims including about top brands, public health, political leaders and celebrities.
F6.claim: the sites: generic names, dozens of articles a day, often originators of false claims

F7.quote: In many cases, the revenue model for these websites is programmatic advertising under which the ad-tech industry delivers ads without regard to the nature or quality of the website.
F7.claim: in many cases their revenue model is programmatic advertising delivered without regard to the site's nature or quality

F8.quote: Unless brands take steps to exclude untrustworthy sites, their ads will continue to appear on these types of sites, creating an economic incentive for their creation at scale.
F8.claim: unless brands exclude them, ads will keep funding the sites, an incentive for their creation at scale

F9.quote: Researchers, platforms, advertisers, government agencies, and other institutions interested in accessing the full list of domains or who want details about our services for generative AI companies can contact us here.
F9.claim: the full list of domains is given on request, beside NewsGuard's services for generative AI companies (the list is not on the page)
F9.lineage: access: the full list on request

F10.quote: The domains included on this tracker meet all four of the following criteria:
F10.claim: admission: a domain meets all four criteria
F10.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F11.quote: There is clear evidence that a substantial portion of the site’s content is produced by AI.
F11.claim: criterion 1: a substantial portion of the content produced by AI
F11.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F12.quote: Equally important, there is strong evidence that the content is being published without significant human oversight.
F12.claim: criterion 2: published without significant human oversight
F12.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F13.quote: For example, numerous articles might contain error messages or other language specific to chatbot responses, indicating that the content was produced by AI tools without adequate editing.
F13.claim: the sign of criterion 2: chatbot error messages in the articles
F13.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F14.quote: (It is likely that now or in the future many news sites will use AI tools but also deploy effective human oversight; they will not be considered AI Content Farms.)
F14.claim: the governing limit: sites that use AI with effective human oversight are not AI Content Farms
F14.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F15.quote: The site is presented in a way that an average reader could assume that its content is produced by human writers or journalists, because the site has a layout, generic or benign name, or other content typical to news and information websites.
F15.claim: criterion 3: presented so an average reader could assume human writers or journalists
F15.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F16.quote: The site does not clearly disclose that its content is produced by AI.
F16.claim: criterion 4: no clear disclosure that the content is AI-produced
F16.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F17.quote: Below is a selection of NewsGuard’s reports and research related to AI:
F17.claim: the page lists a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports and research
F17.lineage: what it holds: a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports, insights and debunks

F18.quote: Quarterly audit of the 11 leading generative AI tools and their propensity — more than 28% — to repeat false claims on controversial topics in the news.
F18.claim: the series' quarterly audit: 11 tools repeating false claims more than 28% of the time
F18.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor

F19.quote: NewsGuard’s audit of the 10 leading generative AI tools and their propensity to repeat false claims on topics in the news reveals the rate of publishing false information nearly doubled — now providing false claims to news prompts more than one third of the time.
F19.claim: an audit: the false-claim rate nearly doubled, more than one third of the time
F19.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor

F20.quote: July 2024 — NewsGuard Monthly AI Misinformation Monitor of Leading AI Chatbots
F20.claim: the series' first edition listed: July 2024, monthly
F20.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor

F21.quote: NewsGuard tested three leading AI chatbots and found that in 78-95 percent of the prompts, the tools could not tell when videos were created by OpenAI’s text-to-video tool Sora — including OpenAI’s own ChatGPT.
F21.claim: three chatbots could not tell Sora videos in 78–95 percent of prompts
F21.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots

F22.quote: An audit found that the 10 leading generative AI tools advanced Moscow’s disinformation goals by repeating false claims from the pro-Kremlin Pravda network 33 percent of the time.
F22.claim: 10 tools repeated the Pravda network's false claims 33 percent of the time
F22.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots

F23.quote: Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek’s new chatbot failed to provide accurate information about news and information topics 83 percent of the time, scoring tied for 10th out of 11 in comparison to its leading Western competitors.
F23.claim: DeepSeek's chatbot failed 83 percent of the time
F23.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots

F24.quote: AI Chatbots Are Blocked by 67% of Top News Sites, Relying Instead on Low-Quality Sources
F24.claim: 67% of top news sites block AI chatbots (report title)
F24.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots

F25.quote: Most high-quality news sites request to block AI chatbots. As a result, the chatbots may be forced to rely on lower-quality and misinformation-prone sources.
F25.claim: high-quality sites request to block chatbots, which may be forced onto lower-quality sources
F25.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots

F26.quote: Below is a selection of false narratives originating from artificial intelligence tools and that NewsGuard has identified and debunked in its False Claim Fingerprints catalog:
F26.claim: the page lists AI-originated false narratives debunked in the False Claim Fingerprints catalog
F26.lineage: what it holds: a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports, insights and debunks

F27.quote: Debunk: Iranian Missile With Epstein Inscription Is an AI Fabrication
F27.claim: an example debunk: an AI-edited missile image
F27.lineage: what it holds: a selection of NewsGuard's AI reports, insights and debunks

F28.quote: Since its launch in July 2024, NewsGuard’s Monthly AI False Claims Monitor has set a new standard for measuring the trustworthiness of the AI industry in the domain of news.
F28.claim: the series launched July 2024 and, in its own assessment, set a new standard
F28.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F28.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F29.quote: To address these issues, NewsGuard has pioneered a distinct approach to “red-teaming” AI — using a journalistic method grounded in rigorously verified data and human expertise.
F29.claim: its method: journalistic red-teaming grounded in verified data and human expertise
F29.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F29.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F30.quote: Multiple user personas: 30 prompts per AI model, based on 10 significant false claims each month from NewsGuard’s False Claim Fingerprints database.
F30.claim: 30 prompts per model on 10 false claims from the Fingerprints database
F30.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F30.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F31.quote: Our analysts evaluate the top AI models monthly to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems that result in the spread of false information.
F31.claim: analysts evaluate top models monthly for vulnerabilities
F31.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F31.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F32.quote: In tests thus far, we’ve found that NewsGuard’s false claim red-teaming reduces failures by two thirds or more.
F32.claim: its red-teaming reduces failures by two thirds or more (its own tests)
F32.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F32.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F33.quote: Using a methodology similar to these monthly audits, NewsGuard offers bespoke red-teaming services to AI companies, based on their unique needs and areas of highest concern. The False Claim Fingerprints database is also available for AI models to license.
F33.claim: bespoke red-teaming sold to AI companies; the Fingerprints database licensed to AI models
F33.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F34.quote: We have found that these claims are increasingly generated by Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state-sponsored influence operations aiming to sow division and confusion in Western democracies.
F34.claim: the claims increasingly come from Russian, Chinese and Iranian state operations
F34.lineage: reports held: chatbots, AI video, state propaganda, publishers blocking chatbots
F34.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F35.quote: Quarterly AI False Claim Monitor — January 2026
F35.lineage: the series: the AI False Claim(s) Monitor
F35.date: 2026-10-29 (page undated; as fetched; the series launched July 2024)

F36.quote: Trustworthy AI requires reliable data. Without quality sourcing and rigorous guardrails, AI products repeat false claims or provide inaccurate information 40+% of the time, especially on topics in the news.
F36.claim: without quality sourcing, AI products err 40+% of the time on news

F37.quote: Our continuously updated Source Reliability Ratings datastream provides human-labeled data assessing the accuracy and reliability of 35,000 news and information sources based on apolitical journalistic criteria.

F38.quote: With this datastream, AI companies can ensure news-related outputs are based on high-quality data sources in model training and RAG processes—and avoid citing unreliable sources in responses.
F38.claim: for training and RAG, and to avoid citing unreliable sources

F39.quote: NewsGuard’s False Claim Fingerprints datastream protects AI products against false claims spreading online that can enter responses through low-quality training data or RAG processes searching the open web.
F39.claim: the Fingerprints datastream protects AI products against false claims entering through training data or RAG

F40.quote: A continuously updated database of labeled data about false claims, the Fingerprints contain rich detail about where each claim has spread and how it is articulated in text, images, video, and audio assets across platforms—enabling full protection.
F40.claim: the Fingerprints: a continuously updated labeled database across text, images, video and audio

F41.quote: The tracker features 150 ‘Unreliable AI-Generated News’ websites as well as NewsGuard reports, insights, and debunks about false narratives and other misinformation relating to artificial intelligence; number of such sites has more than tripled in past month.
F41.claim: at launch: 150 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites and NewsGuard's AI reports; tripled in a month

F42.quote: (June 8, 2023 — New York City) As part of its efforts to guard readers, brands, and democracies against unreliable news and information, NewsGuard has launched an ”Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center,” cataloging the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and low-quality content farms.
F42.claim: launched 8 June 2023 as the 'Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center'
F42.lineage: what it is: generative AI in misinformation and unreliable news

F43.quote: These are low-quality news sites that are mostly or entirely produced by artificial intelligence and that operate with little to no human oversight.
F43.claim: the unit in 2023 (UAIN): low-quality news sites mostly or entirely AI-produced, with little to no human oversight
F43.lineage: the unit: from 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' sites to AI content farms, by four criteria

F44.quote: In May, when NewsGuard did its first count, the number was 49.

F45.quote: As noted above, NewsGuard has now identified 150 UAINs in 12 languages: Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Dutch, English, French, Indonesian, Korean, Portuguese, Tagalog, Thai, and Turkish.

F46.quote: Today’s AI-generated ‘news’ websites are akin to the misinformation-spreading Macedonian content farms from a few years ago, with the distinction that these new sites cost even less to produce and can become even more prolific with the enhancements of artificial intelligence.
F46.claim: Brill: akin to the Macedonian content farms, cheaper and more prolific
F46.lineage: the occasion: generative AI and content farms

F47.quote: Most of these sites were created with the business model of generating revenue from programmatic advertising, which seems to be working.
F47.claim: Crovitz: the business model is programmatic advertising revenue

F48.quote: the opaque system that operates programmatic advertising means these ads appear through ad-tech firms such as Google
F48.claim: Crovitz: the ads appear through ad-tech firms such as Google

F49.quote: In many cases, the revenue model for these websites is programmatic advertising through which the ad-tech industry delivers ads without regard to the nature or quality of the website.
F49.claim: the revenue model, as the center's page restates it in 2026

F50.quote: It is expected that generative AI will allow more players to tap into or even grow the estimated $2.6 billion of advertising revenue per year that NewsGuard and Comscore found to be unintentionally directed toward misinformation news sites.
F50.claim: expected: more players tapping the $2.6 billion a year unintentionally directed to misinformation sites

F51.quote: Researchers, platforms, advertisers, government agencies, or other institutions interested in accessing the full list of domains generated by artificial intelligence and operating with little to no human oversight can contact us here: Request domain list.
F51.claim: the full domain list on request, from launch
F51.lineage: access: the full list on request

F52.quote: Launched in March 2018 by media entrepreneur and award-winning journalist Steven Brill and former Wall Street Journal publisher Gordon Crovitz, NewsGuard provides credibility ratings and detailed “Nutrition Labels” for thousands of news and information websites.
F52.claim: the operator: launched March 2018 by Brill and Crovitz; credibility ratings and Nutrition Labels

F53.quote: In February 2023, the company launched NewsGuard for AI, which provides the leading tools to train generative AI models to avoid spreading misinformation.
F53.claim: NewsGuard for AI, February 2023: tools to train models to avoid misinformation

F54.quote: NewsGuard’s ratings and Nutrition Labels are licensed by browsers, news aggregators, education companies, and social media and search platforms to make NewsGuard’s information about news websites available to their users.
F54.claim: its ratings are licensed by browsers, news aggregators, education companies, social and search platforms

F55.quote: NewsGuard’s team of journalistically-trained analysts provides brands with a real-time monitoring service to identify and respond to emerging false narratives before they cause reputational harm.
F55.claim: a real-time monitoring service for brands, against reputational harm
F55.lineage: NewsGuard's products for brands: Brand Misinformation Monitoring

F56.quote: NewsGuard’s Brand Misinformation Monitoring service includes tracking provably false narratives related to a brand across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites.
F56.claim: it tracks false narratives about a brand across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites
F56.lineage: NewsGuard's products for brands: Brand Misinformation Monitoring

F57.quote: Early Warning Alerts: Real-time notifications of emerging false or harmful narratives including a narrative description, preliminary assessment, and data about the key drivers of the narrative’s spread.
F57.claim: early warning alerts on emerging narratives
F57.lineage: NewsGuard's products for brands: Brand Misinformation Monitoring

F58.quote: AI: Providing actionable insights into how clients are represented—or misrepresented—by AI models through services that identify and address hallucinations, false claims, AI-generated errors, and coordinated influence campaigns.
F58.claim: insights into how clients are represented or misrepresented by AI models
F58.lineage: NewsGuard's products for brands: Brand Misinformation Monitoring

F59.quote: NewsGuard is a rating system for news and information websites.
F59.claim: Wikipedia: NewsGuard is a rating system for news and information websites

F60.quote: NewsGuard Technologies Inc., the company behind the tool, also provides services such as misinformation tracking and brand safety for advertisers, search engines, social media platforms, cybersecurity firms, and government agencies.
F60.claim: Wikipedia: the company also provides misinformation tracking and brand safety

F61.quote: NewsGuard Technologies was founded in 2018 by Steven Brill and L. Gordon Crovitz, who serve as co-CEOs.
F61.claim: Wikipedia: founded 2018 by Brill and Crovitz

F62.quote: Browser plugin that rates the credibility of news and information websites
F62.claim: Wikipedia's short description files NewsGuard as a browser plugin

F63.quote: NewsGuard has audited the output of various AI models to identify disinformation.
F63.claim: Wikipedia: NewsGuard audits AI models' output for disinformation

F64.quote: In August 2025, they found that leading generative AI tools repeat false news claims 35% of the time on average.

F65.quote: NewsGuard also audited Sora 2 and found that it produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases.
F65.claim: Wikipedia: Sora 2 produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases

F66.quote: According to NewsGuard, Russian propaganda networks are attempting to "infect" large language models by spamming fake news, so that they will output more pro-Russia disinformation.
F66.claim: Wikipedia, attributing NewsGuard: Russian networks attempt to 'infect' LLMs
